rationale: The same hub-first discovery concept increased independent opportunity weeks in three separate calendar years without changing downstream V1.9 underwriting rules.
Across the six incremental selections, all were positive over 60 trading days and five beat CSI300.
The effect is strongest on opportunity recall/frequency, not on improving the return distribution of already-discovered legacy selections.
All three experiments use public generalist-news proxies rather than a complete professional terminal archive, so the evidence is encouraging but not terminal-grade.
The next clean test should use an untouched year and preserve the source-layer rule exactly; do not add sector identities or outcome-derived search terms.
